:JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- for the death of Sri. D.G. Govinda Raja Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
1 Swamy S/o Late S.D. Govindaraju in a Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 06.12.2019 at about 7.45 p.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Govinda Raja Swamy was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-EG-8314 from Wipro Junction towards Sony World Junction and when he reached near 80 feet road, Koramangala, Bengaluru, at that SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3078/2020 time, one BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle from behind.
Due to the impact, Govinda Raja Swamy had sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the said Govinda Raja Swamy had taken to St.John's Hospital,
but, in spite of best treatment, he was succumbed to the injuries on 07.01.2020.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical treatment of the deceased.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Branch Manager at Oriental Insurance Company and was drawing a salary of Rs.1,20,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Govinda Raja Swamy, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832.
Therefore, the Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the SCCH 15 4 MVC No.3078/2020 Petitioners.

5. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondent, Respondent appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement inter-alia denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus and also the injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and the death caused from the said accident.
Further, it contended that no accident has taken place on the alleged date.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

6. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that D.G. Govinda Raja Swamy S/o Late S.D.
Govindaraju sustained injuries due to rash and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3078/2020 negligent act of driving of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832 on dated 06.12.2019 at about 7.45 p.m. and succumbed to injuries?
2) Whether the Petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
2 3)

Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased D.G.
Govinda Raja Swamy S/o Late S.D. Govindaraju?
4) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
5) What Order or Award ?
7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Further, PW.1 has examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked six documents at Ex.P14 to 20 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand, Respondent has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked one SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3078/2020 document at Ex.R1 and closed its side evidence.
8.

During the course of argument ts the Learned counsel for the Respondent has relied on the Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.6624/2017 (MV-D) and another Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.3361/2019 (MV-D).

9. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of written arguments of the Respondent and depositions, documents exhibited and the materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.5 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioners that D.G.Govinda Raja Swamy was died in the accident that SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3078/2020 occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832 by its driver.
11. On the other hand, the Respondent had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC Bus by its driver.
12. The Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
13. The PW1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P13.
Ex. P-1

and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the complaint lodged by the son of the deceased by name Thanmay, the Adugodi Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B) and 187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P3 is the Spot mahazar with Sketch which shows that the Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
3 concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3078/2020 Ex.P4 and 5 are the IMV reports which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.

Ex.P-6 is the Certified copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the Adugodi Traffic Police have submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the BMTC Bus for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B) and 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P7 to 11 are the Aadhaar cards, PAN card, Voter ID and DL of the deceased.
Ex . P12
is the Death Certificate.
Ex.P13 is the PM report which shows the cause of death is due to Septicemia and as a result of multiple injuries sustained.

14. PW-1 has also examined Assistant Manager by name Vidya Shankar as P.W.2 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.P.14 to 20 i.e., Authorization letter, Forwarding Letter, Appointment Letter,
Employees Profile, Benefits of Claim, Appointment to the cadre of Assistant, Group Insurance.
15. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3078/2020 Learned Counsel for the Respondent.
But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent has examined its driver by name Ramesh S. Maradi as RW.1.

He got marked the Certified Copy of the Judgment in CC No. 1933/2020 on the file of MMTC Court,
Bengaluru.
In the cross examination, RW.1 admitted that the FIR and Charge sheet was filed against him.
He also admitted that the accident spot is the busy road and the bus stop was situated 100 feet away from the accident spot.
Though the Ex.R1 shows that, the accused is acquitted in the Criminal case, the same cannot be considered while dealing with the claim Petition.
This case will be tried independently.
The charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Police documents points out the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC Bus by its SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3078/2020 driver and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."

16. Issue No.2 to 4:- All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
17.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased Govinda Raja Swamy.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of Petitioner No.1 and deceased and Voter ID of Petitioner No.2 at Ex.P.7, 8 and 10.
The said documents shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Govinda Raja Swamy, they entitled for the compensation.

18. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 49 years and deceased was working as a Branch Manager at Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and was drawing Rs.1,20,000/- per SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3078/2020 month.

In this regard, PW.1 has examined Assistance Manager as PW.2 and she produced Authorization letter, Forwarding Letter, Appointment Letter, Employees Profile,
Benefits of Claim, Appointment to the cadre of Assistant, Group Insurance at Ex.P14 to 20.

Upon going through the Ex.P18 i.e., Statement of Gratuity which also contain the Pay slip of the deceased Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
4 which shows the Basic pay is Rs.58,825/- and D.A is Rs. 38,236.25/- totally amounting to Rs.
97,061/-.

The Income Tax deduction shows Rs.12,840/- and the Professional Tax shows Rs. 200/-
which totally amounting to Rs. 13,040/-.
If we deduct Rs. 13,040/- from Rs. 97,061/- then it comes to Rs. 84,021/-.

Hence the monthly income of the deceased to be taken at Rs.84,021/- p.m.
19.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Govinda Raja Swamy as 49 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.8 and Ex.P17 i.e., the Aadhaar card and Employee's Profile of the deceased Govinda Raja Swamy which shows his date of birth as 13.04.1968.
The alleged SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3078/2020 accident was occurred on 06.12.2019.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Govinda Raja Swamy was 51 years, 7 months and 24 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Govinda Raja Swamy to be taken at 52 years for the purpose of assessment.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
21.
The deceased has left behind him his wife and son.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased.
PW.1 in her cross examination deposed that her son ie., Petitioner No.2 is working in Delhi.
Hence, it is clear that Petitioner No.2 is major and not the dependent on the income of the deceased.
The Petitioner no.1 being the wife only SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3078/2020 dependent on the deceased

. At this juncture, I would like to go through the principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

22 . As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the wife and son of the deceased Govinda Raja SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3078/2020 Swamy, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
5 23.

entities.text: Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 is the son, he lost his father's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
24. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3078/2020 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:

25. It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was taken at Rs.84,021/- pm.
26.

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: In case permanent employee or on fixed salary the addition should be 15% when the age is between 50 to 60 years".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 52 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 15% of the income has to be added.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.96,624/- p.m.
(Rs.84,021/- + R.12,603/- = Rs.96,624/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 11.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per detailed discussion made SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3078/2020 above, this tribunal holds that Petitioner No.1 is only the dependent on the deceased.
Hence, 50% of the income of the deceased to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

27. After deducting 50% towards his personal expenses in Rs.96,624/-, it comes to Rs.48,312/-
(Rs.96,624/- - 48,312/-) and multiplier applied is 11 which comes to Rs.63,77,184/- (48,312 x 12 x 11).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.63,77,184/- towards loss of dependency.

28. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 96,800/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/-
5. Expenses of transportation of Rs. 5,000/-

 Total Rs. 65,65,284/-

sentences.text: Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.65,65,284/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

29. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0832.
In this case, the Respondent is the R.C. Owner cum Internal Insurer of BMTC bus.
Therefore, the Respondent has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 "In the Affirmative" and Issue No.4 "Partly in the Affirmative".
30. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3078/2020 Rs.65,65,284/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.65,65,284/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners and directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3078/2020 1) 90% to the Petitioner No.1 Rashmi Swamy vs B.M.T.C on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151478664/
7 2) 10% to the Petitioner No.2

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50%
each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively by way of E-payment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
